questions.q: Which data type should you use to store only a Salesforce record's ID, without the rest of the record?
questions.explain: A Text variable is the right fit for storing just a record's ID as a string, not the whole record.

questions.q: What must a Boolean variable use to represent true or false, per this lesson?
options: The literal words "true" and "false" typed as text
The True and False global constants
questions.explain: Boolean variables must use Flow's True/False global constants — typing the literal words is read as text, not a value.

questions.q: What does a Record variable hold that a Text or Number variable cannot?
options: Every field value from one Salesforce record at once, each in its own data type
Nothing — a Record variable is identical to a Text variable
questions.explain: A Record variable holds all of a record's field values together, each keeping its own data type, just like the real record.

questions.q: Where does a record-triggered flow get its first record variable from, without you building it by hand?
options: It's automatically given once you select the object at the Start element
You must always create it manually from the Toolbox first
It comes from a Text Template
It's copied from a different flow's Debug run
questions.explain: Once you select the triggering object at Start, Salesforce automatically gives the flow a record variable holding the triggering record.

questions.q: On the Create Records screen, what does "How to set record field values" let you choose between?
options: Setting values manually, or copying them from an existing record variable
questions.explain: Create Records lets you set the new record's fields manually, one at a time, or from an existing record variable.
